static_traits.name: Li Jin
static_traits.family_status: Has four siblings, oneself is the youngest (the baby of the family)
static_traits.social_status: Has friends and family to communicate with, but they may not fully understand the Fear of physical challenges; interpersonal and occupational functioning Not mentioned.
static_traits.medical_history: Lost an arm in a car accident years ago; no other important physical illness; no similar psychological problems before the accident, never received counseling treatment.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, Good logic; negative-leaning and skeptical tone, but able to cooperate; able to concretely describe Fear, avoidance and attempts; willing to try gradually and observe changes.

basic_info.main_problem: After losing an arm in a car accident, I fear being unable to complete challenging hiking routes.
basic_info.core_demands: I now decide to seek counseling because this fear is limiting my experience and causing frustration.
growth_experiences: A car accident years ago cost an arm, the accident was very stressful; since then, the client developed strong Fear when facing physically demanding tasks (e.g., high-difficulty hiking), worrying about being unable to complete and failing in front of others; therefore gradually avoiding new, difficult physical challenges, outdoor activities significantly reduced, self-confidence affected. No similar problems before the accident, also never received counseling treatment.

core_beliefs: I cannot complete physically demanding tasks
Failure will make me appear weak in front of others and be judged

special_situations.event: When considering trying a new, difficult hiking route
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the task is hard and requires strength, I will likely be unable to complete it, and will lose face in front of others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids difficult challenges in advance, or only chooses smaller, easier tasks to reduce the risk of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may never finish the whole route

special_situations.event: Imagining the situation of physical difficulty during hiking, being unable to continue halfway
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once physical problems appear, I will be trapped, unable to move forward or back, the consequences will be terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Relying on others' help or giving up in advance to avoid falling into a worse state
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be trapped halfway, things will get out of hand

special_situations.event: Recalls completing a short hike with friends a few months ago, then thinks of a harder route
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the task is harder, past successful experiences do not count, cannot show I am capable of handling bigger challenges
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Only focusing on risks and shortcomings, ignoring available evidence and existing successes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That time was just luck, no help for harder challenges

special_situations.event: When traveling with friends, worries about failing or appearing weak in front of them
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I rest or seek help, others will think I cannot do it, very weak
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Choosing to tough it out alone or simply not participating in challenging activities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I cannot do it, looking down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to restore ability, complete physical challenges, and be accepted and recognized by others
core_conflict.fear: Fears failing in challenges, appearing weak in front of others, and being judged
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of failure and shame and maintains a sense of safety by avoiding difficult tasks or choosing only small challenges

object_relations.self_representation: A self that easily fails and is limited in the face of physical challenges
object_relations.object_representation: Others/bystanders who may judge or not understand one's Fear

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests gradually taking on challenges by setting small goals, or when facing starting a new difficult hiking plan
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think these methods may not work for oneself; once trying fails, will lose face in front of others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a gentle, stable, Empathetic tone, first validating their worries and Sense of frustration; using open questions and concrete probing to Guide reality testing and evidence gathering; positively restating their past small successes and available support, emphasizing controllable pacing and choice, avoiding confrontation and judgment.

manifestations: After the accident-caused disability, experiencing limited freedom of action, the Fear of physical challenges expanding into self-limitation
Worries that failing in front of others leads to self-restraint and avoidance
outcomes: Avoids difficult hikes and physical tasks
Reduced outdoor activities and limited experiences
Decreased confidence and increased Sense of frustration

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Before starting new challenges, excessively worries about failure and others' judgment
Emphasizing 'I cannot do it''may not finish', repeatedly weighing whether to do it and how
Skeptical about support and rest strategies; cautious and hesitant

exception_events.target_problem: When considering trying physically demanding high-difficulty hiking, the client usually Anticipates giving up halfway and failing in front of others, thus choosing Avoiding challenges.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few months ago did a short hike with a friend; this time did not avoid as before, but completed the whole course and felt a sense of achievement afterward.
exception_events.reason: Different support: having a friend accompany and assist; different approach: choosing a shorter, less difficult route with more attainable goals; lighter load making emotional pressure bearable.

positive_force: Willing to try and gradually challenge (already has small-scale practice)
Social support from family and friends
Has had one successful short-distance hiking experience, which can serve as evidence and a resource
Has the motivation to carry out reality testing and behavioral experiments
negative_force: Catastrophic and predictive cognition (worries about giving up halfway and being trapped)
The avoidance pattern Reinforced Fear and failure scripts
Worry about others' evaluations and shame
Actual pressure and uncertainty brought by limited physical function (losing an arm)

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids more difficult hiking and other physically challenging tasks
antecedent: Seeing or planning difficult hiking routes
Friends invite or thinking of tackling harder routes with others
Imagining the situation of physical exhaustion halfway, being unable to continue
target_behavior.core_reason: Losing an arm in the car accident formed strong Fear of failure and others' judgment, accompanied by catastrophic and predictive Automatic thoughts, lowering Self-efficacy
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and shame, maintaining subjective safety and controllability
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced outdoor activities, limited experiences; Decreased confidence and increased Sense of frustration; life satisfaction affected
